Promoting Fundamental British Values

Children are encouraged to regard people of all faiths, races and cultures with respect and tolerance and understand that while different people may hold different views about what is ‘right’ and ‘wrong’, all people living in Britain are subject to its law.

Welcome
'Happy, Safe and Full of Learning'
On behalf of the staff and governors, I welcome you to Park Walk Primary School’s website. It has been designed to help prospective parents or carers find out more about our school and is full of information for our current families.
Park Walk is a vibrant, inclusive and happy one-form entry primary school for children from four to 11 years old, with on site provision for little children aged between 6 months and 3 years in our Seedlings Nursery. In January 2025, Park Walk joined the Fox Federation - a group of five local schools and a Nursery working together in order to provide the very best educational and enrichment experiences for all our children.
Our team of dedicated and friendly staff are very proud of the children who attend Park Walk, recognising all of their achievements in the classroom and beyond. We celebrate every child’s successes and through a stimulating and exciting curriculum, foster a thirst for knowledge; a love of learning and a deep curiosity about the world around them. Our school motto 'Happy, Safe and Full of Learning' underpins everything we do and the children at Park Walk are joyful learners, who are inquisitive and work hard to reach the challenges set by the staff.
Please contact the school office if you would like any further information or would like to arrange a visit. In the meantime, please feel free to browse our website, our weekly newsletters which are published here, and our school's instagram account: parkwalkprimary to get a feel for life at our lovely school.
Kate Webster, Head of School

Breakfast Club
Park Walk Primary School Breakfast Club
Join us for a nutritious and fun start to the school day!
Our qualified staff will plan stimulating activities and provide care for each child. The children will be encouraged to be independent, helping with the preparation of food, choosing activities, and tidying away afterward.
You must book and pay for a place in advance via SCOPAY
You must arrive between 8 – 8.15 a.m. (no entry after 8.15 a.m.)
Cost - £2 per day (sibling/s charged at £1 per day)
Breakfast Club will be held in the School Hub.
Children will be offered a healthy breakfast to ensure they have a great start to the day. There shall be a variety of cereal, toast, yogurts, fruit, and milk on offer.

Curriculum
As part of the Fox Federation, Park Walk follows the Federation’s well-established, research-informed curriculum, which has been consistently recognised for its excellence by a range of external partners and professionals.
At the heart of every subject lies the core principle that children should master key skills and knowledge at each stage, applying what they have learned in different contexts; making meaningful connections with prior learning and building secure foundations before progressing to new concepts.
At Park Walk, staff carefully adapt and implement the Federation curriculum to reflect the needs, interests and strengths of our children, ensuring every child achieves their very best.
English: Reading & Writing At Park Walk, children become confident readers and writers who use language with purpose and enjoyment in a wide range of contexts. Oracy underpins every aspect of learning: children learn to express themselves clearly, explain their thinking and listen to others. These strong foundations in spoken language support their progress in reading, writing and across the wider curriculum. Our teaching helps children see themselves as authors and thinkers, developing curiosity about language and ideas.
Children in our Early Years begin their reading journey with Essential Letters and Sounds (ELS), a systematic phonics programme that helps them learn to read confidently and accurately. ELS is being introduced across the school and will replace Read Write Inc. in Years 1 and 2. Our phonics lessons ensure that every child builds secure foundations for fluency, comprehension and a lifelong love of reading.
Maths Maths at Park Walk is designed to help every child develop confidence and curiosity as they build secure knowledge and understanding. Through a balance of fluency, reasoning and problem-solving, children learn to make sense of numbers, patterns and relationships, helping them make connections to the world around them.
Science Science at Park Walk encourages children to ask questions, explore and make sense of the world around them. Through practical enquiry and discussion, they learn to think critically and use evidence to explain their ideas. Our children grow into curious, informed citizens who understand how science shapes their lives and the planet’s future.
Computing Our computing curriculum, which is delivered through Purple Mash software helps children to understand how technology works and how to use it safely and creatively. They learn to problem-solve, code and communicate responsibly in a digital world as well as how to critically analyse content online. Throughout their time at Park Walk, children develop into competent users of technology who know how to create, connect and stay safe online.
Art & Design Art at Park Walk gives every child the chance to explore, create and express ideas visually. Children experiment with materials and techniques while learning about artists from a wide range of backgrounds. Their finished pieces show imagination, individuality and developing technical skill.
Design & Technology Through designing, making and evaluating, children learn to turn their ideas into purposeful, creative solutions. They explore how things work; use tools safely and consider sustainability in what they design. Park Walk children become inventive, resourceful thinkers who take pride in making things that matter.
Geography helps our children make sense of the world, its people, places and environments. They learn to ask thoughtful questions, use maps and data, and understand how human choices affect the planet. Through carefully planned teaching of both substantive knowledge (the facts and concepts of geography) and disciplinary knowledge (how geographers think and work), our curriculum helps children build a strong sense of place and curiosity about the world, alongside a deep understanding of their responsibility to protect and care for it.
History History at Park Walk brings the past to life through stories, enquiry and connection. Children learn about different periods, people and perspectives, developing a sense of identity and understanding of change over time. Children are encouraged to think critically about evidence and discuss how history shapes who we, and our communities, are today.
Music Music is a joyful part of school life at Park Walk. Every child learns to listen, perform and compose, discovering the power of rhythm, melody and teamwork. Through singing and playing together each week, children build confidence, concentration and a genuine love of music.
Physical Education (PE) We want every child to enjoy being active, develop coordination and build resilience through physical activity. PE at Park Walk promotes teamwork, respect and a sense of achievement through sport and movement. Children develop an understanding of healthy habits, confidence and an understanding of how physical exercise supports mental wellbeing.
PSHE We help children understand themselves, others and the world and how to make good choices, stay safe and show kindness. Through discussion, reflection and real-life contexts, they learn about relationships, rights and responsibilities. Our children grow into thoughtful, confident and compassionate members of their community.
Religious Education (RE)
RE at Park Walk helps children explore beliefs, traditions and values in a respectful and thoughtful way. They learn about different religions and worldviews, and from them by reflecting on the meaning and relevance of these ideas in their own lives. Through asking big questions and appreciating diversity, children build empathy, understanding and a sense of belonging in our multicultural world.
Please visit the Federation Curriculum page for further information.

Special Education Needs and Disability (SEND) at Park Walk
At Park Walk, we ensure that children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) are supported, regardless of their specific needs, to make the best possible progress and achieve their potential in school. We ensure that all children are included in all areas of the curriculum, with the needs of SEND children carefully considered. We have a graduated approach to SEND, ensuring early identification of needs and a continuum of support for children in order to enable them to make progress. Please refer to our SEND Policy on the policies page, which outlines the purpose, nature and management of special educational needs within our school.
Overview of our Provision
At Park Walk Primary School, approximately 12% of children are on the SEND register. The majority of learning needs will be met through Quality First Teaching - ie through the usual lessons delivered by the class teacher with very carefully planned adaptations to the provision within the classroom based on the particular needs of the child.
Where children need additional support, we have a comprehensive intervention programme. Our staff are trained to provide interventions, where necessary, covering various curriculum areas. These include
As part of the Local Offer, we have support from our Educational Psychologist, Speech and Language Therapist, Occupational Therapist, CAHMs Support Worker, MIND practitioner and School Nurse. We also receive support from the Autism and Early Years Intervention Team, the SEND Inclusive Education Team and the Behaviour Intervention Team as part of our extended SEND support.
Follow this link for RBKC’s Local Offer to gain a better understanding of the Local Offer:
We have a SEND Governor, who meets regularly with our SENDCo and the team of Federation SENDCos to supports the school in ensuring we meet the needs of all children with additional and special needs.
The information on our website complies with the Special Educational Needs Code of Practice 2014 and is in line with the Special Educational Needs and Disability Regulations 2014. This information is updated annually and any change to information occurring during the year is updated as soon as possible.
If you would like detailed information regarding our SEND Provision at Park Walk, please refer to the Policies page.
Alternatively, you can contact our SEND coordinator, Amy Formosa, or our Head of School, Kate Webster via email on info@parkwalk.rbkc.sch.uk
Admissions for children with an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP):
The Local Authority will send the school copies of the child’s most recent EHCP which outlines the child’s needs. The school will assess the child’s needs and will consult with the local authority to determine whether the school can meet the child’s needs. We strongly encourage parents / carers of children with EHCPs to visit the school and speak with the SENDCo if you are thinking of naming us in your child’s plan. This will allow us the opportunity to meet and discuss any questions and concerns you want to address in order for you to determine the most appropriate setting for your child
Admissions for children with additional needs and SEND:
If your child has additional needs or has SEND but no EHCP, please apply via the local authority route’s normal admissions procedure. We still strongly encourage you to visit the school to have the appropriate discussions about your child’s needs and the suitability of the school to support your child.

Admissions at Seedlings Nursery
We are very proud of the provision in our lovely Seedlings Nursery and would love the opportunity to show you around if you are thinking of us for your little one.
Please contact the school office on 0207 352 8700 or email info@parkwalk.rbkc.sch.uk
We offer high quality childcare for children aged 6 months – 3 years old.
Our Acorns provision is for children aged 6 months – 2 years.
Our Sunflowers provision is for children aged 2 - 3 years.
Most of our Seedlings children continue onto our Park Walk Nursery Class in the year they turn four. Subject to primary school admissions criteria, the vast majority of these children then continue into our Reception Class and beyond.
Seedlings nursery has an amazing team of Nursery Practitioners who have years of valuable experience, working with children. They are compassionate and have a caring approach to childcare. This is evident in the bonds made between them and the children. We ensure all the staff in our setting are in receipt of an enhanced DBS check, trained in safeguarding and hold a first aid qualification.
We provide a calm, caring and safe learning space where each child can flourish and fulfil their full potential. We promote independence and confidence by encouraging children to explore the variety of activities we have through which they learn to share and discover new abilities and interests. Our weekly timetable is enhanced with specialist extracurricular teachers to ensure learning is extended, both in and out of the classrooms.
Some of our additional activities include:
All meals (Breakfast, Snack, Lunch and Tea appropriate to attended hours) are provided
Pureed food, milk, nappies and wipes must be supplied by each family for under 2s
